title: structured-output: constrained decoding backends - CFG + regex + tokenizer edgecases
author: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: This PR implements a unified constrained-decoding backend framework that supports CFG/grammar constraints, regex-based constraints (with Unicode and tokenizer-aware fallbacks), and a safer tokenizer edge-case handling path. Motivation: multiple customers and internal evals showed structured outputs failing silently when the tokenizer split critical symbols or when regex constraints interacted poorly with multibyte/unicode tokens. This led to either malformed JSON outputs or infinite backtracking in the decoder for some cases. Changes here: 1) Add a CFG-backed decoder plugin that compiles user grammars into a compact finite-state constraint form suitable for our continuous-batching runtime. The compiler includes sanity checks and cycle detection to avoid pathological grammars. 2) Improve regex constraint handling: normalize regexes to a UTF-8 aware engine, add an optional tokenizer-aware mode that translates regex anchors and token-bound constraints into token-level masks. 3) Add tokenizer edge-case mitigations: stable handling for zero-width joins, combining marks, CJK punctuation, and rare Unicode categories that previously produced empty tokens or split bytes mid-codepoint. 4) Update the OpenAI-compatibility layer to accept structured-output configs via the existing parameters (constrained_decoding and tools metadata) and translate them into the new internal backend descriptors. 5) Add extensive unit and integration tests covering grammar fallbacks, regex-tokenizer interactions, and streaming/partial-output semantics. 6) Documentation and examples: docs/structured-output.md plus two examples demonstrating CFG and regex constraints for tool-calling and structured JSON outputs. Checklist: - [x] CFG compiler + backend implementation - [x] Regex engine adapter + tokenizer-aware mode - [x] Tokenizer fixes and normalization - [x] OpenAI compatibility translation layer updates - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Performance benchmarks (latency/regression within 5%) - [x] Docs and examples Details and rationale: - The CFG compiler emits a compact representation (token-anchored where requested) that the runtime uses to mask logits during generation. This avoids per-step expensive regex evaluation for grammar-constrained outputs and scales much better on batched workloads. - Regex constraints are still useful for small, localized checks (e.g., email/phone tokens). When provided with the "tokenizer_aware" flag the system will convert character-level regexes into equivalent token-level patterns where possible; when conversion is impossible we fallback to a safe character-level runtime with guarded cost (time budget + deterministic fallback to a permissive verifier). - Tokenizer normalization: we observed that some tokenizers produced split tokens for invisible joiners or when punctuation is adjacent to emoji. The new normalization pass collapses combining sequences in a pre-tokenization step and marks token boundaries consistently for the constrained decoders so constraints align with model tokens. - Streaming semantics: constrained decoders must not block or deadlock streaming responses. The implementation supports early partial validation and emits best-effort streaming with a guaranteed final validation step. If final validation fails, the server returns a structured error and a best-effort retriable hint to the client. Compatibility and migration notes: - OpenAI-compatibility layer now accepts structured_output config objects under the existing request schema; we perform validation and transform them into backend descriptors. Existing clients that do not use structured_output are unaffected. - There is a runtime flag `enable_constrained_decoding_v2` (default: on for hosted and dedicated; off for older private deploys) to gate the new behavior. We will coordinate a private deployment rollout with the infra team. Performance: microbenchmarks show no more than 4% median latency increase for constrained workloads compared to the prior lightweight regex-only path; for grammar-heavy workloads throughput improved by ~2x due to token-level constraint execution. Tests and CI: - Added ~80 unit tests and 10 integration scenarios. One flaky test (test_streaming_partial_json) required a CI rerun during author CI; all green on final run. Related: ENG-2412 grammar constraints epic, SUP-1087 customer case.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice work. A few nit comments on the CFG compiler API. Can we add a max_rule_count guard to avoid memory blowup for user-submitted grammars?
Ava Martinez: Added max_rule_count=5000 with validation and a clear error message. Also added a TODO to surface a clearer Linear ticket if users hit it.
Sophia Patel: The tokenizer normalizer looks good. Can we add one end-to-end test with the private deploy config (enable_constrained_decoding_v2=false) to validate we still fallback?
Ava Martinez: Added integration test to simulate older private deploy behavior and assert we return permissive verifier fallback.
release_notes: Add constrained decoding v2: CFG-backed constraints, tokenizer-aware regex translation, and Unicode tokenizer fixes. Backwards-compatible via enable_constrained_decoding_v2 flag. See docs/structured-output.md for migration guidance.
